paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the God who lets hard things come is the same God who sets a limit on them. Isaiah 10:24-25 says the Lord GOD of Hosts tells His people, "do not fear Assyria," because "in just a little while My fury against you will subside." Assyria looked like the biggest thing in the room. But a rod only swings as long as the One holding it allows. And Isaiah says the yoke will be broken (Isaiah 10:27).

Now look at who the remnant ends up leaning on. Isaiah 10:20 says they will "no longer depend on him who struck them, but they will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel." Think about that. How many of us keep running back to the very thing that hurt us, hoping THIS time it'll treat us right? The remnant's story is about learning to rely on the right One, and Isaiah 10:21 says a remnant of Jacob will return to the Mighty God.

And friend, a remnant is not a leftover. Isaiah 10:22 says Israel's people may be like the sand of the sea, and still only a remnant will return. That's heavy, so I won't joke about it. But the Lord keeps a people for Himself, and Lebanon's tall trees fall before the Mighty One (Isaiah 10:34), so you don't have to be big or tall to be held by Him. This isn't the end of Isaiah's message, so keep your oven warm.
